prompt: Complete the generic Pair<T> class: store two values of type T, provide getFirst() and getSecond(), and implement swapped() to return a new Pair with the values exchanged.
explanation: The type parameter T lets one Pair class work for any element type, so Pair<String> and Pair<Integer> both compile with full type safety. Fields, constructor parameters, and return types all use T just like a normal type name. swapped() demonstrates an immutable style: instead of mutating its own fields, it builds and returns new Pair<>(second, first), leaving the original untouched.
hints: Declare the fields as private T first; and private T second; -- T works anywhere a type name would.
The getters simply return the matching field.
In swapped(), do not modify this pair. Return new Pair<>(second, first); the compiler infers the type argument.
